# Adjudication Task — Chapter 535

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃535화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|“매 대협. 아니 맹주께서 찾으신다.”
  6|
  7|갑작스러운 진위경의 말에 순간 멈칫한 내가 되물었다.
  8|
  9|“저를 말입니까?”
 10|
 11|“그래. 그리고 청 소협도 함께.”
 12|
 13|나에 이어 청풍까지?
 14|
 15|진위경에게 그 이유를 물어보려던 찰나, 전각에 나 있는 창에서 익숙한 얼굴이 불쑥 튀어나왔다.
 16|
 17|“할아버지! 지금 할아버지 만나러 가요?”
 18|
 19|기대가 잔뜩 담긴 청풍의 외침에, 희미하게 웃은 진위경이 작게 고개를 저었다.
 20|
 21|“자네의 조부님이 아니라, 맹주께서 찾으시는 거라네.”
 22|
 23|“네. 그러니까 할아버지요!”
 24|
 25|“같지만 다르지. 여하튼 청 소협도 조속히 채비해서 내려오게.”
 26|
 27|“잠시만요! 만두 좀 챙기고요!”
 28|
 29|“그래, 골고루 챙기게. 당과도.”
 30|
 31|짬밥 좀 먹었나. 눈 하나 깜빡하지 않는 것 보소.
 32|
 33|진위경도 청풍을 한두 번 본 것이 아니라 그런지, 이제는 대처가 물 흐르듯 자연스럽다.
 34|
 35|청풍이 우당탕탕 소리를 내며 사라지자 진위경의 시선이 나를 향했다.
 36|
 37|“이유를 묻지 않는구나.”
 38|
 39|“……물어볼 틈이 없었다는 게 정확한 것 같은데요.”
 40|
 41|“그것도 그렇군.”
 42|
 43|“어차피 이렇게 된 거, 가서 직접 듣겠습니다. 사실 벌써 느낌이 살짝 오긴 했거든요.”
 44|
 45|“무슨 느낌?”
 46|
 47|“음, 손주 얼굴이나 보려고 부르진 않았을 것 같다는 느낌이죠.”
 48|
 49|나와 청풍을 찾는다.
 50|
 51|검성 매종학이, 아니. 무림맹의 맹주가.
 52|
 53|같은 사람이지만 어떤 이름이냐에 따라 의미가 다르다. 앞서 진위경이 청풍의 호칭을 정정했던 것은 그런 뜻이 내포되어 있을 것이다.
 54|
 55|‘무림맹주.’
 56|
 57|그 이름은 무겁다. 그리고 구주(九州)를 종횡하는 수많은 무림인과 천하 무림을 양쪽 어깨에 짊어진 거인이 나를 보고자 한다는 건…….
 58|
 59|‘아무리 생각해도 쎄한데.’
 60|
 61|그새 또 다른 사건이 터진 걸까.
 62|
 63|내심 그렇게 생각하고 있던 바로 그때였다.
 64|
 65|쉬이이익!
 66|
 67|바람 부는 소리와 함께 청풍이 모습을 드러냈다. 손에는 빵빵하게 부풀어 오른 비단 보자기가 들려 있었고, 상반신에는 번쩍거리는 은빛 갑옷을 걸친 채였다.
 68|
 69|잠깐. 갑옷?
 70|
 71|취릭.
 72|
 73|“이제 왔. 뭐여, 시벌.”
 74|
 75|“미미요. 쑥쑥 커 버려서 이제 품 안에 못 넣고 다녀요.”
 76|
 77|“……그럼 두고 가는 건 어때.”
 78|
 79|청풍이 고개를 갸웃거렸다.
 80|
 81|“왜요?”
 82|
 83|“지금 진심으로 몰라서 묻는 거야?”
 84|
 85|“네!”
 86|
 87|“오…… 대답 한 치의 망설임도 없는 것 봐. 환장하겠네.”
 88|
 89|뱀이다. 그냥 뱀도 아닌 뿔 달린 뱀.
 90|
 91|이제 미미라는 이름이 잘못되었다고 느껴질 만큼 떡대도 상당하다.
 92|
 93|결론만 말하자면, 무림맹에 뱀 애호가가 몇 명이나 있을지는 몰라도 딱히 환영받을 만한 반려 뱀은 아니라는 거지.
 94|
 95|“……도대체 얘한테 뭘 먹인 거야?”
 96|
 97|“헤헤. 엄청 많이 컸죠. 은인이 맞춰 보세요.”
 98|
 99|나는 망설임 없이 대답했다.
100|
101|“스테로이드.”
102|
103|“주로 만두랑 당과 먹였는데요. 아, 혈어(血魚)를 먹인 이후로 확실히 엄청 커진 것 같긴 해요.”
104|
105|도대체 뱀한테 만두랑 당과를 왜 먹이냐고 따지려던 나는 멈칫했다.
106|
107|“혈어?”
108|
109|“네.”
110|
111|혈어는 동정호를 통해 마력에 오염된 물고기들이다.
112|
113|그럼 한마디로 단단히 상한 음식을 먹었다는 건데…….
114|
115|“안 되겠다. 미미는 두고 가.”
116|
117|“괜찮은데요.”
118|
119|“다른 사람이 안 괜찮아. 물 수도 있잖아.”
120|
121|“아니에요. 미미는 물라고 해도 안 물어요. 보실래요?”
122|
123|다급한 표정을 지은 청풍이 미미를 향해 손을 뻗었다.
124|
125|“미미, 물어!”
126|
127|쐐액, 딱!
128|
129|그야말로 순식간이었다.
130|
131|아가리를 쩍 벌린 미미가 번개처럼 쇄도하고, 그보다 빠른 속도로 청풍의 손이 사라졌다.
132|
133|텅 빈 허공을 향해 이빨을 딱 부딪친 미미가 아쉽다는 듯 혀를 날름거렸다.
134|
135|취릭.
136|
137|“보세요. 안 물죠?”
138|
139|“…….”
140|
141|“…….”
142|
143|미친놈인가.
144|
145|‘아니, 이건 그냥 못 문 거잖아.’
146|
147|나를 포함한 모두가 할 말을 잃은 그때, 청풍이 울상이 된 얼굴로 중얼거렸다.
148|
149|“살, 아니 문경이가 괜찮다고 했는데…….”
150|
151|“문경이가?”
152|
153|“네. 요새 자주 보거든요. 그때 미미 상태도 살펴봤어요.”
154|
155|그러고 보니 요새 통 청풍과 문경이 눈에 잘 띄지 않았다. 내가 바쁜 탓도 있었겠지만, 자주 본다는 청풍의 말을 들어보니 그것 때문만은 아닌 것 같다.
156|
157|‘다른 사람한테는 관심도 안 주던 인간이. 갑자기 무슨 바람이 불어서?’
158|
159|가늘어지는 내 눈초리를 본 청풍이 헛숨을 삼켰다.
160|
161|“헙.”
162|
163|“왜?”
164|
165|“아니에요. 아무것도.”
166|
167|이렇게 나오니까 더 수상쩍은데.
168|
169|하지만 나는 어깨를 으쓱하는 것으로 상황을 마무리했다. 진위경이 슬슬 초조해지기 시작하는 것이 눈에 보였기 때문이다.
170|
171|“막내야, 그.”
172|
173|“아, 죄송해요. 많이 급합니까?”
174|
175|“솔직히 늦어서 좋을 건 없겠지. 다른 분들도 함께 기다리고 계실 테니.”
176|
177|다른 분들?
178|
179|이거 생각보다 판이 제법 큰 모양이다.
180|
181|나는 껄끄러운 마음을 숨기며 청풍을 향해 턱짓했다.
182|
183|“가자, 청 소협.”
184|
185|“네, 은인!”
186|
187|궁기방과 혁무진이 굳은 얼굴로 고개를 끄덕였다.
188|
189|“그래, 가 보자고.”
190|
191|“제가 모시겠습니다, 조장님. 그리고 소가주님.”
192|
193|“너희 둘은 개소리하지 말고 남아서 때랑 똥이나 닦아.”
194|
195|“…….”
196|
197|“…….”
198|
199|
200|
201|* * *
202|
203|
204|
205|하나의 작은 도시를 연상케 하는 무림맹.
206|
207|그중에서도 중심에 우뚝 선 맹주전(盟主殿)에 들어선 우리는 커다란 문 앞에 섰다.
208|
209|“오셨군요.”
210|
211|경직된 눈빛과 표정. 그리고 잘 갈무리된 기세.
212|
213|의심의 여지 없이 검기상인(劒氣傷人)의 경지에 오른 절정 고수지만, 이 이름 모를 사내의 역할은 문지기에 불과하다.
214|
215|이미 진위경과는 일면식이 있는지, 나지막한 인사를 건넨 그가 문을 열었다.
216|
217|드르륵. 드르륵. 드르륵.
218|
219|차례차례 울리는 마찰음. 그렇게 자그마치 다섯 개의 문이 열리고 나서야 보이는 광경에, 나는 내심 중얼거렸다.
220|
221|‘그놈들 놔두고 오길 잘했네.’
222|
223|궁기방과 혁무진은 나한테 감사해야 한다.
224|
225|따라왔다면 아마 이 자리에서 악취와 똥 냄새를 풍기며 입 벙긋 못한 채 식은땀만 줄줄 흘렸을 테니까.
226|
227|그만큼 거대한 탁자를 두고 자리한 이들의 면면과 기세는 대단했다.
228|
229|“와아.”
230|
231|옆에서 자그마한 탄성이 흘러나온다. 눈을 동그랗게 뜬 채 주위를 둘러보는 청풍의 옆구리를 쿡 찌른 진위경이 전음을 흘려보냈다.
232|
233|- 난 여기까지다.
234|
235|무슨 뜻인지 알아듣기에는 충분하다.
236|
237|고개를 끄덕인 나는 문턱을 넘어 걸음을 내디뎠다.
238|
239|저벅.
240|
241|고요한 적막 속에서 울려 퍼지는 발걸음.
242|
243|그와 동시에 날카롭고, 덤덤하며, 한편으로는 경탄과 호기심이 어린 시선들이 나와 청풍을 향해 쏟아진다.
244|
245|“허어. 바로 저 아이들이 말로만 듣던…….”
246|
247|“다시 봐도 대단합니다.”
248|
249|“흠. 제법이긴 하군.”
250|
251|“무슨 소리. 실로 대단한 일이오. 무림 전체의 홍복이 아닐 수 없소.”
252|
253|좌우로 흘러나오는 늙수그레한 목소리의 주인들.
254|
255|지고한 경지의 무공에 도달하여 노화를 더디게 만들었음에도 하나 같이 새하얗게 흰 터럭은 그들이 흘려보낸 시간을 짐작게 하기에 충분했다.
256|
257|‘구파일방. 그리고 오대세가의 장문인과 가주들.’
258|
259|천하 무림을 떠받치는 열다섯 개의 기둥.
260|
261|무림의 전국구 이벤트라고 부를 수 있는 성라대연 때도 그들 모두가 모인 적은 없었다.
262|
263|심지어 무림맹이 선포되던 숭산결의 때조차 그랬다. 워낙 거리가 먼 탓에 일정에 맞춰 도착하지 못한 이들이 있었기 때문이었다.
264|
265|하지만 드디어…….
266|
267|‘모두가 한자리에 모였다.’
268|
269|성라대연이 이제 막 떠오르기 시작한 별들의 잔치였다면, 이 자리는 유구한 무림 사에 자신만의 이름과 족적을 아로새긴 거인(巨人)들의 연회다.
270|
271|그리고 이 연회에서도 단연 거대한 존재감을 뿜어내는 몇 사람이 있었다.
272|
273|더 이상 일가(一家)의 가주가 아님에도 그 이상의 영향력을 발휘하는 그들을, 천하의 무림인들은 경의를 담아 이렇게 불렀다.
274|
275|일신(一神), 삼성(三星), 십왕(十王).
276|
277|과거, 붉게 물든 서쪽 하늘을 등지고 중원을 향하여 쏘아진 십만의 마군(魔軍)이 있었고, 그에 맞선 영웅들이 있었다.
278|
279|그들은 적을 가르는 검과 창이었고, 중원을 수호하는 방패였으며, 마침내는 거대하고도 빛나는 신화가 되었다.
280|
281|무신이라는 하늘이 사라지자 하늘을 빛내던 세 개의 별들이 하나둘씩 자취를 감추었고, 스스로 왕좌에서 내려온 열 명의 왕들은 서서히 죽거나 늙었지만 그중 일부는 이 자리로 돌아왔다.
282|
283|‘창천검왕, 벽력도왕. 그리고…….’
284|
285|낯익은 얼굴도, 낯선 얼굴도 있다.
286|
287|그리고 그중에서도 가장 눈에 띄는 한 사람이 나를 보며 눈썹을 들썩였다.
288|
289|- 부른 지가 언젠데 이제야 오다니. 네놈이 죽고 싶어서 환장했구나.
290|
291|화왕 적천강.
292|
293|퉁명스럽지만 따뜻함이 담긴 그의 전음에, 나도 모르게 소리 없는 웃음이 흘러나온다.
294|
295|- 이놈 보게. 지금 웃음이 나오느냐?
296|
297|그럼 나오는 걸 어떡합니까.
298|
299|- 하여간 그놈 참. 방금까지는 잔뜩 굳어 있더니. 구파일방이나 오대세가나. 어차피 별거 없다. 전부 거기서 거기야. 본문이 최고지.
300|
301|그 누가 이렇게 거침없이 말할 수 있을까.
302|
303|당당하면서도 광오한 한마디에 이어, 짧은 망설임이 담긴 전음이 귓가에 닿았다.
304|
305|- 그러니까 어깨 펴고 눈 부릅떠라. 네놈은…… 노부의 자긍심이다.
306|
307|자긍심.
308|
309|생각지도 못한 말이다.
310|
311|비록 소리내어 말하지는 않았지만, 적천강이 내게 이런 말을 할 것이라고는 예상치 못했다.
312|
313|나는 참지 못하고 입술을 달싹였다.
314|
315|- 노야.
316|
317|슬쩍 시선을 회피하고 있던 적천강의 신형이 움찔했다.
318|
319|- 크흠.
320|
321|- 노야.
322|
323|- 왜, 왜 부르느냐.
324|
325|- 약 드실 시간 같아서요.
326|
327|- 이런 개호로…….
328|
329|- 그리고 감사합니다.
330|
331|- ……!
332|
333|적천강의 붉은 눈썹이 파르르 떨렸다.
334|
335|그에게서 시선을 뗀 나는 허리를 꼿꼿하게 폈다.
336|
337|어느새 긴장으로 굳어 있던 전신의 근육이 부드럽게 이완되고 눈앞이 시원해진다.
338|
339|‘난 누군가의 자긍심이다.’
340|
341|아직 이 자리가 무엇을 위해 마련된 것인지 모르겠다.
342|

[P126]

[P127]
*They’re all here.*

[P128]
If the Star-Array Grand Banquet was a feast for stars just beginning to rise, this was a banquet for giants who had carved their names and left their marks on Murim’s long history.

[P129]
Even among them, a few presences stood out.

[P130]
They no longer headed their families, yet wielded even greater influence. Martial artists throughout the land spoke of them with reverence:

[P131]
One God, Three Saints, Ten Kings.

[P132]
Long ago, a hundred thousand demonic soldiers had been sent toward the Central Plains with the blood-red western sky at their backs. Heroes had stood against them.

[P133]

[P134]

[P135]
*The Azure Sky Sword King. The Thunderbolt Saber King. And…*

[P136]

[P137]
*—How long has it been since I called for you? Only showing up now? You must be desperate to die.*

[P138]
Fire King Jeok Cheongang.

[P139]

[P140]
*—Look at you. You can smile at a time like this?*

[P141]
*What am I supposed to do if I feel like smiling?*

[P142]
*—Honestly. You were stiff as a board a moment ago. The Nine Sects and One Gang, the Five Great Families—none of them are anything special. They’re all much the same. Our sect is the best.*

[P143]

[P144]

[P145]

[P146]
*Pride.*

[P147]

[P148]

[P149]

[P150]
*—Old Master.*

[P151]

[P152]
*—Ahem.*

[P153]
*—Old Master.*

[P154]

[P155]

[P156]

[P157]

[P158]

[P159]

[P160]

[P161]
*I’m someone’s pride.*

[P162]

[P163]
Step.

[P164]

[P165]

[P166]

[P167]
Silence.

[P168]

[P169]

[P170]
Rattle.

[P172]

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;

Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.

- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.

[P88]
*Others?*

[P89]

[P90]

[P91]
“Let’s go, Young Hero Cheongpung.”

[P92]
“Yes, Benefactor!”

[P93]

[P94]
“Right. Let’s go.”

[P95]

[P96]

[P97]
“…”

[P98]
“…”

[P100]

[P101]

[P102]
“You’ve arrived.”

[P103]
The man guarding it had a rigid expression and a carefully contained aura.

[P104]
He was unmistakably a Peak master who had reached the level of injuring others with Sword Energy. Yet here, this nameless man was only a doorkeeper.

[P105]
He appeared to know Jin Wikyung. After greeting him quietly, he opened the door.

[P106]
Rattle. Rattle. Rattle.

[P107]

[P108]
*Good thing I left those idiots behind.*

[P109]
Gung Gibang and Hyuk Mujin ought to thank me. If they’d followed, they’d be standing here stinking of grime and shit, too scared to open their mouths and sweating buckets.

[P110]
The people seated around the enormous table were that imposing.

[P111]
“Wow.”

[P112]

[P113]
*—This is as far as I go.*

[P114]
I understood. I nodded and stepped over the threshold.

[P115]
Step.

[P116]
My footsteps echoed through the silence.

[P117]
Gazes fell on Cheongpung and me—some sharp, some impassive, others full of wonder and curiosity.

[P118]
“Oh? So these are the youngsters we’ve heard so much about…”

[P119]
“They’re remarkable, even the second time I’ve seen them.”

[P120]
“Hm. Not bad.”

[P121]
“What do you mean, not bad? What they’ve done is extraordinary. A blessing for all of Murim.”

[P122]

[P123]
*The leaders of the Nine Sects and One Gang. And the Family Heads of the Five Great Families.*

[P124]
Fifteen pillars supporting Murim.

[P125]

[P126]

[P127]
*They’re all here.*

[P128]
If the Star-Array Grand Banquet was a feast for stars just beginning to rise, this was a banquet for giants who had carved their names and left their marks on Murim’s long history.

[P129]

[P130]

[P131]
One God, Three Saints, Ten Kings.

[P132]

[P133]

[P134]

*The Azure Sky Sword King. The Thunderbolt Saber King. And…*

[P136]

[P137]
*—How long has it been since I called for you? Only showing up now? You must be desperate to die.*

[P138]
Fire King Jeok Cheongang.

[P139]

[P140]

[P141]

[P142]

[P144]

[P145]

[P146]
*Pride.*

[P147]
I hadn’t expected that word.

[P148]

[P152]

[P153]
*—Old Master.*

[P154]

[P155]

[P156]
*—You little fucking…*

[P157]
*—And thank you.*

[P158]
*—…!*

[P159]
His red eyebrows trembled.

[P160]
I looked away and straightened my back. The muscles that had tightened throughout my body relaxed, and my head cleared.

[P161]
*I’m someone’s pride.*

[P162]
I still didn’t know why this gathering had been called. But I knew one thing: the confidence I had briefly lost, then found again, was what had brought me here.

[P163]
Step.

[P164]
Cheongpung and I stopped together.

[P165]
The corridor that had seemed so long had ended. There was nowhere farther to walk.

[P166]
The giants’ quiet conversations cut off as if they had been waiting for that exact moment.

[P167]
Silence.

[P168]
A silence waiting for one man, made for one man.

[P169]
At the place of honor among those twenty-odd giants, a man rose. Instead of white hair, he had black, and his eyes were clear.

[P170]
Rattle.

[P171]
Three stars had once adorned the sky above the vast world. Of them, the brightest—and now the only one remaining—was Sword Saint Mae Jonghak.

[P172]
He opened his mouth.

[P173]
No.

[P174]
*Alliance Leader Mae Jonghak.*

[P175]
That was the man standing here. And I wasn’t the only one who understood.

[P176]
Cheongpung spoke so softly that only I could hear.

[P177]
“Grandpa…”

[P178]

[P179]
“The masters of the Two Dragons Pavilion have arrived.”

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
